There are multiple ways to sum f : ι → ℕ∞, e.g.

  • tsum f
  • ⨆ s : Finset ι, s.sum f
  • (Cardinal.sum <| Cardinal.ofENat.{0} ∘ f).toENat
  • finsum f

The first one requires importing topology, and the next two don't seem to have API. finsum has a lot of API but very few results for finsum, ENat. It's also 0 instead of ⊤ when the support is infinite. Maybe we should have a version of finsum that works with WithTop M for AddCommMonoid M?
What's the recommended way to sum such a function, in directories where importing topology/reals isn't okay? (recommended = most common, has some API)
Just to spell it out: I expect the sum to be ⊤ when f has infinite support, otherwise it should equal Finset.sum over the support.

(ENNReal does have theorems that show the iSup version coincides with tsum, but they don't exist for ENat. Maybe they're true for any OrderTopology α?)

Maybe we should have a version of finsum that works with WithTop M for AddCommMonoid M?

For this one I think you need something stronger like CanonicallyOrderedAdd, as it doesn't work for Int

Overall I would use tsum as that's feels the closest to the textbook
Oh wait I was thinking something else. tsum doesn't sound the best to me any more...
I no longer have a feeling of which one is good. Maybe you can provide more context so I can tell which I like in a specific context?

There's not much context other than wanting to sum ENats in a way that'll play nice with Set.encard/ENat.card. But to be more specific, I'm thinking about the degree sum formula:

2 * G.edgeSet.encard = ∑ v, G.degree v

where G is a graph which isn't necessarily finite (docs#SimpleGraph.sum_degrees_eq_twice_card_edges is the finite statement). I want this to make sense even when there are infinitely many edges. In this context, the easiest definition to prove it with would be the Cardinal.sum one.

A generalised condition for the iSup formulation might be ConditionallyCompletePartialOrder ENat, ScottContinuous (· + ·), and ∀ n m, n ≤ n + m
(edit: and OrderTop ENat)
btw I just found out about #38326, which uses tsum to define graph degrees

A generalised condition for the iSup formulation

wdym by "condition" here? It can be defined for any AddCommMonoid + SupSet.
Is the definition supposed to work for {-1, 1} : Set ℤ?

The thing ENat and ENNReal have going for them is a very strong convergence condition
(EDIT : namely ∑ i : I, x_i ≤ ∑ i : I ∪ J, x_i)

Chris C said:

Is the definition supposed to work for {-1, 1} : Set ℤ?

If you mean something that doesn't absolutely converge, I think no. But this has finite support (assuming you mean a function from Fin 2), so yeah.
But my question is not "let's invent a new sum function", it's - what are people using right now for these cases? (and especially for ENat)
I might still go with tsum in my casual project, but for mathlib standard I am not sure
docs#ENat.BigOperators would be the right home for relevant results, but it only describes the Finset.sum case
....ditto ENNReal :(

However, as I look at it again, the right way seems to be showing OrderTopology.of_linearLocallyFinite holds for ENat.

btw in addition to the 4 ways in the OP, another way to sum f : ι → ℕ∞ as suggested by Bhavik Mehta is:

  • ENat.card <| Σ i, Set.Iio (f i)

This is pretty similar to the Cardinal.sum way but doesn't directly mention cardinals directly.

I also think we're missing theorems that relate all of these ways to sum things even for Nats, such as a docs#tsum_eq_finsum that doesn't require finite support (because the junk values coincide).
